claims.text: Grants cover tuition fees for undergraduate students.
Grants are for undergraduate students from low-income Scottish households.
Grants are for undergraduate students who are ineligible for Scottish Government tuition fee support.
Grants support eligible second degrees in skills-shortage subject areas.
The grant covers tuition fees up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and cannot progress.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain valid for the entire course duration, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds towards tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree, unless seeking support for a second undergraduate degree.
Applicants eligible for SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loans are expected to use them fully.
Applications will not be considered if the student is eligible for support from Student Finance England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, or any overseas government/agency.
Generally, funding will not cover more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
Applications for different courses after receiving previous funding may not be considered.
Part-time students receiving tuition fee support from SAAS may apply if the SAAS award is less than total fees.
Students who came to Scotland solely to study at university/college without prior Scottish education or ties to Scotland are not eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree may be considered exceptionally for a second undergraduate degree at the discretion of CEF.

Students must have an unconditional offer for, or be continuing on, an undergraduate degree course at a Scottish institution or a course validated by a Scottish university but delivered in Scotland for academic year 2026-27.

HNC, HND, Access courses, accelerated degree courses with graduate entry, courses outside Scotland, courses validated by non-Scottish universities but delivered in Scotland, Open University courses, CPD courses, and university courses below degree level are not eligible.
Postgraduate degrees are not eligible for support.
For second degrees, students must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of the new course.
For second degrees, students must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
For second degrees, students must have been unable to gain employment in their previous degree's subject area, be unemployed, facing redundancy, or have been made redundant.
For second degrees, students must wish to reskill in a different field of study recognized as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
Eligible courses for second degrees are restricted to specific subject areas listed.
No exceptions or exemptions will be made to eligibility criteria.
Students who have already started a second degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026, for grants covering academic year 2026-27.
An eligibility checker must be completed before applying.
Applications are made online.
Late applications will not be accepted unless the student was informed of SAAS ineligibility after the portal closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks if all information and referee responses are timely.
Supporting documents include evidence of eligibility, university acceptance letter, SAAS Award Notice, and P60/pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
